hints: Focus on the characteristic thermal decomposition products of Group 2 metal nitrates: metal oxide, brown nitrogen dioxide gas, and oxygen gas.
Recall the general stoichiometry for Group 2 nitrate decomposition: 2 moles of nitrate decompose to 2 moles of oxide, 4 moles of NO2, and 1 mole of O2.
Check the oxidation state of Group 2 radium (+2) to confirm the formula of radium oxide as RaO.
walkthrough:
**Recall Group 2 nitrate thermal decomposition**

All Group 2 nitrates decompose on strong heating following the same pattern, yielding the solid metal oxide, brown nitrogen dioxide gas, and colorless oxygen gas:

$$2\text{M}(\text{NO}_3)_2(\text{s}) \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2\text{MO}(\text{s}) + 4\text{NO}_2(\text{g}) + \text{O}_2(\text{g})$$

**Apply to radium**

Radium is in Group 2 below barium. Its ion has a $+2$ charge $(\text{Ra}^{2+})$, so the oxide formed is $\text{RaO}$.

**Verify stoichiometric balance**

Substituting radium into the general equation:

$$2\text{Ra}(\text{NO}_3)_2(\text{s}) \rightarrow 2\text{RaO}(\text{s}) + 4\text{NO}_2(\text{g}) + \text{O}_2(\text{g})$$
Reactants: $2 \text{ Ra}, 4 \text{ N}, 12 \text{ O}$.
Products: $2 \text{ Ra}, 4 \text{ N}, 2 + 8 + 2 = 12 \text{ O}$.
The equation is balanced and matches option A.

options.A: Correct. Group 2 nitrates decompose thermally to form the metal oxide, nitrogen dioxide, and oxygen: 2Ra(NO3)2(s) -> 2RaO(s) + 4NO2(g) + O2(g).
options.B: Incorrect. Group 2 nitrates do not decompose to nitrogen gas (N2); nitrogen is released as nitrogen dioxide gas (NO2).
options.C: Incorrect. Group 2 nitrates do not produce dinitrogen monoxide (N2O); the nitrogen product is NO2.
options.D: Incorrect. Radium is in Group 2 and forms Ra2+ ions, so the oxide formula is RaO, not Ra2O (which would correspond to a +1 oxidation state).
